source_register.title: Diplomatic Academy
source_register.notes: Primary-source basis for this initial methodology-development dossier. No private or restricted source was used.

institutional_core.mission: Professional development of MFA officers and relevant public officials through structured diplomatic learning across career stages.
institutional_core.governance: An academy within Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
institutional_core.programme_model: Career-stage programmes including foundation/basic training, pre-posting preparation and management development.
institutional_core.learning_model: Structured diplomatic training incorporating practitioner knowledge, policy discussion and scenario-based methods.
institutional_core.professional_practice_model: Uses simulations, policy gaming and experienced diplomatic practitioners as part of professional preparation.
institutional_core.international_cooperation_model: The official page describes international benchmarking/exchanges and engagement with foreign diplomatic academies and partners.
institutional_core.digital_transparency_model: The official MFA provides a dedicated public Academy page describing its role and training model.
distinctive_practices: use of senior practitioners and external expertise
international benchmarking with other diplomatic academies
methodology_lessons_for_wpa: Career-stage progression is a recurring institutional capability that should be visible within programme architecture and professional-practice evidence.
Simulation and policy-gaming evidence strongly supports keeping practice-based training as a distinct indicator.
Practitioner integration should remain separately visible from general faculty transparency.
International benchmarking is useful evidence of institutional learning, but should not be treated as quality merely because a partnership is claimed.
